malware.name: FinFisher
malware.description: FinFisher is a government-grade commercial surveillance spyware reportedly sold exclusively to government agencies for use in targeted and lawful criminal investigations.

malware.name: FIVEHANDS
malware.description: FIVEHANDS is a customized version of DEATHRANSOM ransomware written in C++. FIVEHANDS has been used since at least 2021, including in Ransomware-as-a-Service (RaaS) campaigns, sometimes along with SombRAT.

malware.name: Flagpro
malware.description: Flagpro is a Windows-based, first-stage downloader that has been used by BlackTech since at least October 2020. It has primarily been used against defense, media, and communications companies in Japan.

malware.name: Flame
malware.description: Flame is a sophisticated toolkit that has been used to collect information since at least 2010, largely targeting Middle East countries.

malware.name: FLASHFLOOD
malware.description: FLASHFLOOD is malware developed by APT30 that allows propagation and exfiltration of data over removable devices. APT30 may use this capability to exfiltrate data across air-gaps.

malware.name: FlawedAmmyy
malware.description: FlawedAmmyy is a remote access tool (RAT) that was first seen in early 2016. The code for FlawedAmmyy was based on leaked source code for a version of Ammyy Admin, a remote access software.

malware.name: FlawedGrace
malware.description: FlawedGrace is a fully featured remote access tool (RAT) written in C++ that was first observed in late 2017.

malware.name: FLIPSIDE
malware.description: FLIPSIDE is a simple tool similar to Plink that is used by FIN5 to maintain access to victims.

malware.name: FoggyWeb
malware.description: FoggyWeb is a passive and highly-targeted backdoor capable of remotely exfiltrating sensitive information from a compromised Active Directory Federated Services (AD FS) server.

malware.name: Fooder
malware.description: Fooder is a custom 64-bit C/C++ loader used by MuddyWater that can decrypt and reflectively load embedded payloads such as a go-socks5 proxy utility, the open-source HackBrowserData infostealer, or the MuddyViper…

malware.name: Forfiles
malware.description: Forfiles is a Windows utility commonly used in batch jobs to execute commands on one or more selected files or directories (ex: list all directories in a drive, read the first line of all files created yesterday, etc.).

malware.name: FRAMESTING
malware.description: FRAMESTING is a Python web shell that was used during Cutting Edge to embed into an Ivanti Connect Secure Python package for command execution.

malware.name: FrameworkPOS
malware.description: FrameworkPOS is a point of sale (POS) malware used by FIN6 to steal payment card data from sytems that run physical POS devices.

malware.name: FRP
malware.description: FRP, which stands for Fast Reverse Proxy, is an openly available tool that is capable of exposing a server located behind a firewall or Network Address Translation (NAT) to the Internet.

malware.name: FruitFly
malware.description: FruitFly is designed to spy on mac users .

malware.name: ftp
malware.description: ftp is a utility commonly available with operating systems to transfer information over the File Transfer Protocol (FTP). Adversaries can use it to transfer other tools onto a system or to exfiltrate data.

malware.name: FunnyDream
malware.description: FunnyDream is a backdoor with multiple components that was used during the FunnyDream campaign since at least 2019, primarily for execution and exfiltration.

malware.name: FYAnti
malware.description: FYAnti is a loader that has been used by menuPass since at least 2020, including to deploy QuasarRAT.

malware.name: Fysbis
malware.description: Fysbis is a Linux-based backdoor used by APT28 that dates back to at least 2014.

malware.name: Gazer
malware.description: Gazer is a backdoor used by Turla since at least 2016.

malware.name: Gelsemium
malware.description: Gelsemium is a modular malware comprised of a dropper (Gelsemine), a loader (Gelsenicine), and main (Gelsevirine) plug-ins written using the Microsoft Foundation Class (MFC) framework.

malware.name: GeminiDuke
malware.description: GeminiDuke is malware that was used by APT29 from 2009 to 2012.

malware.name: Get2
malware.description: Get2 is a downloader written in C++ that has been used by TA505 to deliver FlawedGrace, FlawedAmmyy, Snatch and SDBbot.

malware.name: gh0st RAT
malware.description: gh0st RAT is a remote access tool (RAT). The source code is public and it has been used by multiple groups.

malware.name: GLASSTOKEN
malware.description: GLASSTOKEN is a custom web shell used by threat actors during Cutting Edge to execute commands on compromised Ivanti Secure Connect VPNs.

malware.name: GlassWorm
malware.description: GlassWorm is a worm that propagated through supply chain attacks by compromising repository credentials from victim environments and having malicious payloads added to those compromised accounts for distribution to…

malware.name: GLOOXMAIL
malware.description: GLOOXMAIL is malware used by APT1 that mimics legitimate Jabber/XMPP traffic.

malware.name: GoBear
malware.description: GoBear is a Go-based backdoor that abuses legitimate, stolen certificates for defense evasion purposes. GoBear is exclusively linked to Kimsuky operations.

malware.name: Gold Dragon
malware.description: Gold Dragon is a Korean-language, data gathering implant that was first observed in the wild in South Korea in July 2017.

malware.name: GoldenSpy
malware.description: GoldenSpy is a backdoor malware which has been packaged with legitimate tax preparation software. GoldenSpy was discovered targeting organizations in China, being delivered with the "Intelligent Tax" software suite…

malware.name: GoldFinder
malware.description: GoldFinder is a custom HTTP tracer tool written in Go that logs the route a packet takes between a compromised network and a C2 server.

malware.name: GoldMax
malware.description: GoldMax is a second-stage C2 backdoor written in Go with Windows and Linux variants that are nearly identical in functionality.

malware.name: Gomir
malware.description: Gomir is a Linux backdoor variant of the Go-based malware GoBear, uniquely assoicated with Kimsuky operations.

malware.name: Goopy
malware.description: Goopy is a Windows backdoor and Trojan used by APT32 and shares several similarities to another backdoor used by the group (Denis). Goopy is named for its impersonation of the legitimate Google Updater executable.

malware.name: Gootloader
malware.description: Gootloader is a Javascript-based infection framework that has been used since at least 2020 as a delivery method for the Gootkit banking trojan, Cobalt Strike, REvil, and others.

malware.name: Grandoreiro
malware.description: Grandoreiro is a banking trojan written in Delphi that was first observed in 2016 and uses a Malware-as-a-Service (MaaS) business model. Grandoreiro has confirmed victims in Brazil, Mexico, Portugal, and Spain.

malware.name: GravityRAT
malware.description: GravityRAT is a remote access tool (RAT) and has been in ongoing development since 2016. The actor behind the tool remains unknown, but two usernames have been recovered that link to the author, which are "TheMartian"…

malware.name: Green Lambert
malware.description: Green Lambert is a modular backdoor that security researchers assess has been used by an advanced threat group referred to as Longhorn and The Lamberts.

malware.name: GreyEnergy
malware.description: GreyEnergy is a backdoor written in C and compiled in Visual Studio. GreyEnergy shares similarities with the BlackEnergy malware and is thought to be the successor of it.

malware.name: GRIFFON
malware.description: GRIFFON is a JavaScript backdoor used by FIN7.

malware.name: GrimAgent
malware.description: GrimAgent is a backdoor that has been used before the deployment of Ryuk ransomware since at least 2020; it is likely used by FIN6 and Wizard Spider.

malware.name: gsecdump
malware.description: gsecdump is a publicly-available credential dumper used to obtain password hashes and LSA secrets from Windows operating systems.

malware.name: Guard
malware.description: According to Kaspersky Labs, Guard is a malware developed by threat actor WildPressure. It is written in Python and packaged using PyInstaller, both for Windows and macOS operating systems.

malware.name: GuLoader
malware.description: GuLoader is a file downloader that has been used since at least December 2019 to distribute a variety of remote administration tool (RAT) malware, including NETWIRE, Agent Tesla, NanoCore, FormBook, and Parallax RAT.

malware.name: H1N1
malware.description: H1N1 is a malware variant that has been distributed via a campaign using VBA macros to infect victims. Although it initially had only loader capabilities, it has evolved to include information-stealing functionality.

malware.name: Hacking Team UEFI Rootkit
malware.description: Hacking Team UEFI Rootkit is a rootkit developed by the company Hacking Team as a method of persistence for remote access software.

malware.name: HALFBAKED
malware.description: HALFBAKED is a malware family consisting of multiple components intended to establish persistence in victim networks.

malware.name: HAMMERTOSS
malware.description: HAMMERTOSS is a backdoor that was used by APT29 in 2015.

malware.name: Hancitor
malware.description: Hancitor is a downloader that has been used by Pony and other information stealing malware.

malware.name: Hannotog
malware.description: Hannotog is a type of backdoor malware uniquely assoicated with Lotus Blossom operations since at least 2022.

malware.name: HAPPYWORK
malware.description: HAPPYWORK is a downloader used by APT37 to target South Korean government and financial victims in November 2016.

malware.name: HARDRAIN
malware.description: HARDRAIN is a Trojan malware variant reportedly used by the North Korean government.

malware.name: Havij
malware.description: Havij is an automatic SQL Injection tool distributed by the Iranian ITSecTeam security company. Havij has been used by penetration testers and adversaries.

malware.name: Havoc
malware.description: Havoc is an open-source post-exploitation command and control (C2) framework first released on GitHub in October 2022 by C5pider (Paul Ungur), who continues to maintain and develop it with community contributors.

malware.name: HAWKBALL
malware.description: HAWKBALL is a backdoor that was observed in targeting of the government sector in Central Asia.

malware.name: hcdLoader
malware.description: hcdLoader is a remote access tool (RAT) that has been used by APT18.

malware.name: HDoor
malware.description: HDoor is malware that has been customized and used by the Naikon group.

malware.name: HeartCrypt
malware.description: HeartCrypt is a packer-as-a-service (PaaS) used to protect malware that has been available since at least 2024. HeartCrypt has been used to pack a variety of malware including Lumma Stealer, Remcos, and Rhadamanthys.

malware.name: HELLOKITTY
malware.description: HELLOKITTY is a ransomware written in C++ that shares similar code structure and functionality with DEATHRANSOM and FIVEHANDS.

malware.name: Helminth
malware.description: Helminth is a backdoor that has at least two variants - one written in VBScript and PowerShell that is delivered via a macros in Excel spreadsheets, and one that is a standalone Windows executable.

malware.name: HermeticWiper
malware.description: HermeticWiper is a data wiper that has been used since at least early 2022, primarily against Ukraine with additional activity observed in Latvia and Lithuania.

malware.name: HermeticWizard
malware.description: HermeticWizard is a worm that has been used to spread HermeticWiper in attacks against organizations in Ukraine since at least 2022.

malware.name: HexEval Loader
malware.description: HexEval Loader is a hex-encoded loader that collects host data, decodes follow-on scripts and acts as a downloader for the BeaverTail malware. HexEval Loader was first reported in April 2025.

malware.name: Heyoka Backdoor
malware.description: Heyoka Backdoor is a custom backdoor--based on the Heyoka open source exfiltration tool--that has been used by Aoqin Dragon since at least 2013.

malware.name: Hi-Zor
malware.description: Hi-Zor is a remote access tool (RAT) that has characteristics similar to Sakula. It was used in a campaign named INOCNATION.

malware.name: HiddenFace
malware.description: HiddenFace is a modular backdoor developed and used exclusively by MirrorFace since at least 2021. HiddenFace can communicate both actively and passively and has been used against political and academic targets.

malware.name: HiddenWasp
malware.description: HiddenWasp is a Linux-based Trojan used to target systems for remote control. It comes in the form of a statically linked ELF binary with stdlibc++.

malware.name: HIDEDRV
malware.description: HIDEDRV is a rootkit used by APT28. It has been deployed along with Downdelph to execute and hide that malware.

malware.name: Hikit
malware.description: Hikit is malware that has been used by Axiom for late-stage persistence and exfiltration after the initial compromise.

malware.name: Hildegard
malware.description: Hildegard is malware that targets misconfigured kubelets for initial access and runs cryptocurrency miner operations. The malware was first observed in January 2021.

malware.name: HIUPAN
malware.description: HIUPAN (aka U2DiskWatch) is a is a worm that propagates through removable drives known to be leveraged by Mustang Panda and was first observed utilized in 2024.

malware.name: Hive
malware.description: Hive is a strain of ransomware that was first discovered in June 2021. Hive was designed to be used by Ransomware-as-a-service providers, to enable novice cyber-criminals to launch ransomware attacks on healthcare…

malware.name: HOMEFRY
malware.description: HOMEFRY is a 64-bit Windows password dumper/cracker that has previously been used in conjunction with other Leviathan backdoors.

malware.name: HOPLIGHT
malware.description: HOPLIGHT is a backdoor Trojan that has reportedly been used by the North Korean government.

malware.name: HotCroissant
malware.description: HotCroissant is a remote access trojan (RAT) attributed by U.S. government entities to malicious North Korean government cyber activity, tracked collectively as HIDDEN COBRA.

malware.name: HTRAN
malware.description: HTRAN is a tool that proxies connections through intermediate hops and aids users in disguising their true geographical location.

malware.name: HTTPBrowser
malware.description: HTTPBrowser is malware that has been used by several threat groups. It is believed to be of Chinese origin.

malware.name: httpclient
malware.description: httpclient is malware used by Putter Panda. It is a simple tool that provides a limited range of functionality, suggesting it is likely used as a second-stage or supplementary/backup tool.

malware.name: HTTPTroy
malware.description: HTTPTroy is a highly obfuscated backdoor that facilitates collection, command and control, defense evasion and exfiltration. HTTPTroy was first reported in October 2025.

malware.name: HUI Loader
malware.description: HUI Loader is a custom DLL loader that has been used since at least 2015 by China-based threat groups including Cinnamon Tempest and menuPass to deploy malware on compromised hosts.

malware.name: Hydra

malware.name: Hydraq

malware.name: HyperBro
malware.description: HyperBro is a custom in-memory backdoor used by Threat Group-3390.

malware.name: HyperStack
malware.description: HyperStack is a RPC-based backdoor used by Turla since at least 2018. HyperStack has similarities to other backdoors used by Turla including Carbon.

malware.name: IceApple
malware.description: IceApple is a modular Internet Information Services (IIS) post-exploitation framework, that has been used since at least 2021 against the technology, academic, and government sectors.

malware.name: IcedID
malware.description: IcedID is a modular banking malware designed to steal financial information that has been observed in the wild since at least 2017. IcedID has been downloaded by Emotet in multiple campaigns.

malware.name: ifconfig
malware.description: ifconfig is a Unix-based utility used to gather information about and interact with the TCP/IP settings on a system.

malware.name: iKitten
malware.description: iKitten is a macOS exfiltration agent .

malware.name: IMAPLoader
malware.description: IMAPLoader is a .NET-based loader malware exclusively associated with CURIUM operations since at least 2022. IMAPLoader leverages email protocols for command and control and payload delivery.

malware.name: Imminent Monitor
malware.description: Imminent Monitor was a commodity remote access tool (RAT) offered for sale from 2012 until 2019, when an operation was conducted to take down the Imminent Monitor infrastructure.

malware.name: Impacket
malware.description: Impacket is an open source collection of modules written in Python for programmatically constructing and manipulating network protocols.

malware.name: INC Ransomware
malware.description: INC Ransomware is a ransomware strain that has been used by the INC Ransom group since at least 2023 against multiple industry sectors worldwide.

malware.name: Industroyer
malware.description: Industroyer is a sophisticated malware framework designed to cause an impact to the working processes of Industrial Control Systems (ICS), specifically components used in electrical substations.

malware.name: Industroyer2
malware.description: Industroyer2 is a compiled and static piece of malware that has the ability to communicate over the IEC-104 protocol. It is similar to the IEC-104 module found in Industroyer.

malware.name: InnaputRAT
malware.description: InnaputRAT is a remote access tool that can exfiltrate files from a victim’s machine. InnaputRAT has been seen out in the wild since 2016.

malware.name: InvisibleFerret
malware.description: InvisibleFerret is a modular python malware that is leveraged for data exfiltration and remote access capabilities. InvisibleFerret consists of four modules: main, payload, browser, and AnyDesk.

malware.name: InvisiMole
malware.description: InvisiMole is a modular spyware program that has been used by the InvisiMole Group since at least 2013. InvisiMole has two backdoor modules called RC2FM and RC2CL that are used to perform post-exploitation activities.

malware.name: Invoke-PSImage
malware.description: Invoke-PSImage takes a PowerShell script and embeds the bytes of the script into the pixels of a PNG image. It generates a one liner for executing either from a file of from the web.

malware.name: IOControl
malware.description: IOControl is a Linux backdoor compiled for 32-bit ARM devices that has been used to target IoT and OT devices in Israel and the United States, including IP cameras, routers, firewalls, PLCs, HMIs, and Orpak and Gasboy…

malware.name: ipconfig
malware.description: ipconfig is a Windows utility that can be used to find information about a system's TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, and adapter configuration.

malware.name: IPsec Helper
malware.description: IPsec Helper is a post-exploitation remote access tool linked to Agrius operations. This malware shares significant programming and functional overlaps with Apostle ransomware, also linked to Agrius.

malware.name: IronNetInjector
malware.description: IronNetInjector is a Turla toolchain that utilizes scripts from the open-source IronPython implementation of Python with a .NET injector to drop one or more payloads including ComRAT.

malware.name: IronWind
malware.description: IronWind is a custom loader malware that has been in use since at least 2023 by actors including WIRTE to target entities in the Middle East.

malware.name: ISMInjector
malware.description: ISMInjector is a Trojan used to install another OilRig backdoor, ISMAgent.

malware.name: Ixeshe
malware.description: Ixeshe is a malware family that has been used since at least 2009 against targets in East Asia.

malware.name: J-magic
malware.description: J-magic is a custom variant of the cd00r backdoor tailored to target Juniper routers that was first observed during the J-magic Campaign in mid-2023.

malware.name: Janicab
malware.description: Janicab is an OS X trojan that relied on a valid developer ID and oblivious users to install it.

malware.name: Javali
malware.description: Javali is a banking trojan that has targeted Portuguese and Spanish-speaking countries since 2017, primarily focusing on customers of financial institutions in Brazil and Mexico.

malware.name: JCry
malware.description: JCry is ransomware written in Go. It was identified as apart of the #OpJerusalem 2019 campaign.

malware.name: JHUHUGIT
malware.description: JHUHUGIT is malware used by APT28. It is based on Carberp source code and serves as reconnaissance malware.

malware.name: JPIN
malware.description: JPIN is a custom-built backdoor family used by PLATINUM. Evidence suggests developers of JPIN and Dipsind code bases were related in some way.

malware.name: jRAT
malware.description: jRAT is a cross-platform, Java-based backdoor originally available for purchase in 2012. Variants of jRAT have been distributed via a software-as-a-service platform, similar to an online subscription model.

malware.name: JSS Loader
malware.description: JSS Loader is Remote Access Trojan (RAT) with .NET and C++ variants that has been used by FIN7 since at least 2020.

malware.name: JumbledPath
malware.description: JumbledPath is a custom-built utility written in GO that has been used by Salt Typhoon since at least 2024 for packet capture on remote Cisco devices.

malware.name: Kali365
malware.description: Kali365 is a Phishing-as-a-Service (PHaaS) kit first observed in April 2026 that generates victim-targeted lures across multiple operating systems to induce users into copying and pasting actor-controlled commands for…

malware.name: Kapeka
malware.description: Kapeka is a backdoor written in C++ used against victims in Eastern Europe since at least mid-2022. Kapeka has technical overlaps with Exaramel for Windows and Prestige malware variants, both of which are linked to…

malware.name: KARAE
malware.description: KARAE is a backdoor typically used by APT37 as first-stage malware.

malware.name: Kasidet
malware.description: Kasidet is a backdoor that has been dropped by using malicious VBA macros.

malware.name: Kazuar
malware.description: Kazuar is a fully featured, multi-platform backdoor Trojan written using the Microsoft .NET framework.

malware.name: Kerrdown
malware.description: Kerrdown is a custom downloader that has been used by APT32 since at least 2018 to install spyware from a server on the victim's network.

malware.name: Kessel
malware.description: Kessel is an advanced version of OpenSSH which acts as a custom backdoor, mainly acting to steal credentials and function as a bot. Kessel has been active since its C2 domain began resolving in August 2018.

malware.name: Kevin
malware.description: Kevin is a backdoor implant written in C++ that has been used by HEXANE since at least June 2020, including in operations against organizations in Tunisia.

malware.name: KeyBoy
malware.description: KeyBoy is malware that has been used in targeted campaigns against members of the Tibetan Parliament in 2016.

malware.name: Keydnap
malware.description: This piece of malware steals the content of the user's keychain while maintaining a permanent backdoor .

malware.name: KEYMARBLE
malware.description: KEYMARBLE is a Trojan that has reportedly been used by the North Korean government.

malware.name: KEYPLUG
malware.description: KEYPLUG is a modular backdoor written in C++, with Windows and Linux variants, that has been used by APT41 since at least June 2021.

malware.name: KGH_SPY
malware.description: KGH_SPY is a modular suite of tools used by Kimsuky for reconnaissance, information stealing, and backdoor capabilities. KGH_SPY derived its name from PDB paths and internal names found in samples containing "KGH".

malware.name: KillDisk
malware.description: KillDisk is a disk-wiping tool designed to overwrite files with random data to render the OS unbootable. It was first observed as a component of BlackEnergy malware during cyber attacks against Ukraine in 2015.

malware.name: Kinsing
malware.description: Kinsing is Golang-based malware that runs a cryptocurrency miner and attempts to spread itself to other hosts in the victim environment.

malware.name: Kivars
malware.description: Kivars is a modular remote access tool (RAT), derived from the Bifrost RAT, that was used by BlackTech in a 2010 campaign.

malware.name: Koadic
malware.description: Koadic is a Windows post-exploitation framework and penetration testing tool that is publicly available on GitHub.

malware.name: Kobalos
malware.description: Kobalos is a multi-platform backdoor that can be used against Linux, FreeBSD, and Solaris. Kobalos has been deployed against high profile targets, including high-performance computers, academic servers, an endpoint…

malware.name: KOCTOPUS
malware.description: KOCTOPUS's batch variant is loader used by LazyScripter since 2018 to launch Octopus and Koadic and, in some cases, QuasarRAT. KOCTOPUS also has a VBA variant that has the same functionality as the batch version.

malware.name: Komplex
malware.description: Komplex is a backdoor that has been used by APT28 on OS X and appears to be developed in a similar manner to XAgentOSX .

malware.name: KOMPROGO
malware.description: KOMPROGO is a signature backdoor used by APT32 that is capable of process, file, and registry management.

malware.name: KONNI
malware.description: KONNI is a remote access tool that security researchers assess has been used by North Korean cyber actors since at least 2014.

malware.name: KOPILUWAK
malware.description: KOPILUWAK is a JavaScript-based reconnaissance tool that has been used for victim profiling and C2 since at least 2017.

malware.name: Kwampirs
malware.description: Kwampirs is a backdoor Trojan used by Orangeworm. Kwampirs has been found on machines which had software installed for the use and control of high-tech imaging devices such as X-Ray and MRI machines.

malware.name: LAMEHUG
malware.description: LAMEHUG is Python-based information stealer first identified in July 2025 by Ukraine's Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-UA) in phishing emails targeting Ukrainian government officials.

malware.name: Latrodectus
malware.description: Latrodectus is a Windows malware downloader that has been used since at least 2023 to download and execute additional payloads and modules.

malware.name: LaZagne
malware.description: LaZagne is a post-exploitation, open-source tool used to recover stored passwords on a system. It has modules for Windows, Linux, and OSX, but is mainly focused on Windows systems.

malware.name: LazyWiper
malware.description: LazyWiper is a destructive malware observed targeting a manufacturing sector company during the 2025 Poland Wiper Attacks.

malware.name: LightNeuron
malware.description: LightNeuron is a sophisticated backdoor that has targeted Microsoft Exchange servers since at least 2014. LightNeuron has been used by Turla to target diplomatic and foreign affairs-related organizations.

malware.name: LIGHTRAIL
malware.description: LIGHTRAIL is a tunneler malware. LIGHTRAIL has been known to communicate with C2 SOCKS4A Websocket communications. LIGHTRAIL was first observed in 2022.

malware.name: LightSpy
malware.description: First observed in 2018, LightSpy is a modular malware family that initially targeted iOS devices in Southern Asia before expanding to Android and macOS platforms.

malware.name: LIGHTWIRE
malware.description: LIGHTWIRE is a web shell written in Perl that was used during Cutting Edge to maintain access and enable command execution by imbedding into the legitimate compcheckresult.cgi component of Ivanti Secure Connect VPNs.

malware.name: Line Dancer
malware.description: Line Dancer is a memory-only Lua-based shellcode loader associated with the ArcaneDoor campaign. Line Dancer allows an adversary to upload and execute arbitrary shellcode on victim devices.

malware.name: Line Runner
malware.description: Line Runner is a persistent backdoor and web shell allowing threat actors to upload and execute arbitrary Lua scripts. Line Runner is associated with the ArcaneDoor campaign.

malware.name: Linfo
malware.description: Linfo is a rootkit trojan used by Elderwood to open a backdoor on compromised hosts.

malware.name: Linux Rabbit
malware.description: Linux Rabbit is malware that targeted Linux servers and IoT devices in a campaign lasting from August to October 2018. It shares code with another strain of malware known as Rabbot.

malware.name: LiteDuke
malware.description: LiteDuke is a third stage backdoor that was used by APT29, primarily in 2014-2015. LiteDuke used the same dropper as PolyglotDuke, and was found on machines also compromised by MiniDuke.

malware.name: LitePower
malware.description: LitePower is a downloader and second stage malware that has been used by WIRTE since at least 2021.

malware.name: LITTLELAMB.WOOLTEA
malware.description: LITTLELAMB.WOOLTEA is a backdoor that was used by UNC5325 during Cutting Edge to deploy malware on targeted Ivanti Connect Secure VPNs and to establish persistence across system upgrades and patches.

malware.name: Lizar
malware.description: Lizar is a modular remote access tool written using the .NET Framework that shares structural similarities to Carbanak. It has likely been used by FIN7 since at least February 2021.

malware.name: LockBit 2.0
malware.description: LockBit 2.0 is an affiliate-based Ransomware-as-a-Service (RaaS) that has been in use since at least June 2021 as the successor to LockBit Ransomware.

malware.name: LockBit 3.0
malware.description: LockBit 3.0 is an evolution of the LockBit Ransomware-as-a-Service (RaaS) offering with similarities to BlackMatter and BlackCat ransomware.

malware.name: LockerGoga
malware.description: LockerGoga is ransomware that was first reported in January 2019, and has been tied to various attacks on European companies, including industrial and manufacturing firms.

malware.name: LODEINFO
malware.description: LODEINFO is a fileless backdoor malware first identified in 2020 that has been used by actors including MirrorFace, primarily against media, diplomatic, governmental, and public sector organizations in Japan.

malware.name: LoFiSe
malware.description: LoFiSe has been used by ToddyCat since at least 2023 to identify and collect files of interest on targeted systems.

malware.name: LoJax
malware.description: LoJax is a UEFI rootkit used by APT28 to persist remote access software on targeted systems.

malware.name: Lokibot
malware.description: Lokibot is a widely distributed information stealer that was first reported in 2015. It is designed to steal sensitive information such as usernames, passwords, cryptocurrency wallets, and other credentials.

malware.name: LookBack
malware.description: LookBack is a remote access trojan written in C++ that was used against at least three US utility companies in July 2019. The TALONITE activity group has been observed using LookBack.

malware.name: LoudMiner
malware.description: LoudMiner is a cryptocurrency miner which uses virtualization software to siphon system resources. The miner has been bundled with pirated copies of Virtual Studio Technology (VST) for Windows and macOS.

malware.name: LOWBALL
malware.description: LOWBALL is malware used by admin@338. It was used in August 2015 in email messages targeting Hong Kong-based media organizations.

malware.name: LP-Notes
malware.description: LP-Notes is a C/C++ Windows credential stealer used by MuddyWater. LP-Notes was named after the `lp-notes.txt` file that is used to store stolen credentials.

malware.name: Lslsass
malware.description: Lslsass is a publicly-available tool that can dump active logon session password hashes from the lsass process.

malware.name: Lucifer
malware.description: Lucifer is a crypto miner and DDoS hybrid malware that leverages well-known exploits to spread laterally on Windows platforms.

malware.name: Lumma Stealer
malware.description: Lumma Stealer is an information stealer malware family in use since at least 2022. Lumma Stealer is a Malware as a Service (MaaS) where captured data has been sold in criminal markets to Initial Access Brokers.

malware.name: LunarLoader
malware.description: LunarLoader is the loader component for the LunarWeb and LunarMail backdoors that has been used by Turla since at least 2020 including against a European ministry of foreign affairs (MFA).

malware.name: LunarMail
malware.description: LunarMail is a backdoor that has been used by Turla since at least 2020 including in a compromise of a European ministry of foreign affairs (MFA) in conjunction with LunarLoader and LunarWeb.

malware.name: LunarWeb
malware.description: LunarWeb is a backdoor that has been used by Turla since at least 2020 including in a compromise of a European ministry of foreign affairs (MFA) together with LunarLoader and LunarMail.

malware.name: Lurid
malware.description: Lurid is a malware family that has been used by several groups, including PittyTiger, in targeted attacks as far back as 2006.

malware.name: Lynx
malware.description: According to Nextron, Lynx ransomware is a sophisticated malware threat that has been active since mid-2024. Lynx has claimed over 20 victims across a range of industries.

malware.name: Machete
malware.description: Machete is a cyber espionage toolset used by Machete. It is a Python-based backdoor targeting Windows machines that was first observed in 2010.

malware.name: MacMa
malware.description: MacMa is a macOS-based backdoor with a large set of functionalities to control and exfiltrate files from a compromised computer. MacMa has been observed in the wild since November 2021.

malware.name: macOS.OSAMiner
malware.description: macOS.OSAMiner is a Monero mining trojan that was first observed in 2018; security researchers assessed macOS.OSAMiner may have been circulating since at least 2015.

malware.name: MacSpy
malware.description: MacSpy is a malware-as-a-service offered on the darkweb .

malware.name: Mafalda

malware.name: MagicRAT
malware.description: MagicRAT is a remote access tool developed in C++ and exclusively used by the Lazarus Group threat actor in operations.

malware.name: MailSniper
malware.description: MailSniper is a penetration testing tool for searching through email in a Microsoft Exchange environment for specific terms (passwords, insider intel, network architecture information, etc.).

malware.name: Mango
malware.description: Mango is a first-stage backdoor written in C#/.NET that was used by OilRig during the Juicy Mix campaign. Mango is the successor to Solar and includes additional exfiltration capabilities, the use of native APIs, and…

malware.name: Manjusaka
malware.description: Manjusaka is a Chinese-language intrusion framework, similar to Sliver and Cobalt Strike, with an ELF binary written in GoLang as the controller for Windows and Linux implants written in Rust.

malware.name: MarkiRAT
malware.description: MarkiRAT is a remote access Trojan (RAT) compiled with Visual Studio that has been used by Ferocious Kitten since at least 2015.

malware.name: Matryoshka
malware.description: Matryoshka is a malware framework used by CopyKittens that consists of a dropper, loader, and RAT. It has multiple versions; v1 was seen in the wild from July 2016 until January 2017.

malware.name: Maze
malware.description: Maze ransomware, previously known as "ChaCha", was discovered in May 2019. In addition to encrypting files on victim machines for impact, Maze operators conduct information stealing campaigns prior to encryption and…

malware.name: MCMD
malware.description: MCMD is a remote access tool that provides remote command shell capability used by Dragonfly.

malware.name: MechaFlounder
malware.description: MechaFlounder is a python-based remote access tool (RAT) that has been used by APT39. The payload uses a combination of actor developed code and code snippets freely available online in development communities.

malware.name: MEDUSA
malware.description: MEDUSA is an open-source rootkit that is capable of dynamic linker hijacking, command execution, and logging credentials.

malware.name: Medusa Ransomware
malware.description: Medusa Ransomware has been utilized in attacks since at least 2021. Medusa Ransomware has been known to be utilized in conjunction with living off the land techniques and remote management software.

malware.name: meek
malware.description: meek is an open-source Tor plugin that tunnels Tor traffic through HTTPS connections.

malware.name: MegaCortex
malware.description: MegaCortex is ransomware that first appeared in May 2019. MegaCortex has mainly targeted industrial organizations.

malware.name: Megazord
malware.description: Megazord is a Rust-based variant of Akira ransomware that has been in use since at least August 2023 to target Windows environments.

malware.name: Melcoz
malware.description: Melcoz is a banking trojan family built from the open source tool Remote Access PC. Melcoz was first observed in attacks in Brazil and since 2018 has spread to Chile, Mexico, Spain, and Portugal.

malware.name: MESSAGETAP
malware.description: MESSAGETAP is a data mining malware family deployed by APT41 into telecommunications networks to monitor and save SMS traffic from specific phone numbers, IMSI numbers, or that contain specific keywords.

malware.name: metaMain
malware.description: metaMain is a backdoor used by Metador to maintain long-term access to compromised machines; it has also been used to decrypt Mafalda into memory.

malware.name: Metamorfo
malware.description: Metamorfo is a Latin-American banking trojan operated by a Brazilian cybercrime group that has been active since at least April 2018. The group focuses on targeting banks and cryptocurrency services in Brazil and Mexico.

malware.name: Meteor
malware.description: Meteor is a wiper that was used against Iranian government organizations, including Iranian Railways, the Ministry of Roads, and Urban Development systems, in July 2021.

malware.name: MgBot

malware.name: Micropsia
malware.description: Micropsia is a remote access tool written in Delphi.

malware.name: Milan
malware.description: Milan is a backdoor implant based on DanBot that was written in Visual C++ and .NET. Milan has been used by HEXANE since at least June 2020.

malware.name: Mimikatz
malware.description: Mimikatz is a credential dumper capable of obtaining plaintext Windows account logins and passwords, along with many other features that make it useful for testing the security of networks.

malware.name: MimiPenguin
malware.description: MimiPenguin is a credential dumper, similar to Mimikatz, designed specifically for Linux platforms.

malware.name: Miner-C
malware.description: Miner-C is malware that mines victims for the Monero cryptocurrency. It has targeted FTP servers and Network Attached Storage (NAS) devices to spread.

malware.name: Mini Shai-Hulud
malware.description: Mini Shai-Hulud is a credential stealer and self-replicating supply chain worm, derived from Shai-Hulud, that has been used by TeamPCP to target Continuous Integration and Continuous Delivery/Deployment (CI/CD)…

malware.name: MiniBike
malware.description: MiniBike is a custom backdoor written in C++ designed for command execution, data discovery, gathering, and exfiltration. MiniBike has been known to communicate with the C2 using Azure Cloud Infrastructure.

malware.name: MiniBrowse
malware.description: MiniBrowse is a custom stealer designed for the theft of credentials in browsers and passwords stores. MiniBrowse was first observed in late-2025.

malware.name: MiniBus
malware.description: MiniBus is a custom backdoor used for command execution, data discovery, gathering, and exfiltration. MiniBus has utilized Azure Cloud Infrastructure and unique adversary-controlled domains for command and control.

malware.name: MiniDuke
malware.description: MiniDuke is malware that was used by APT29 from 2010 to 2015. The MiniDuke toolset consists of multiple downloader and backdoor components.

malware.name: MiniFast
malware.description: MiniFast is a custom malware designed for long-term persistence and remote code execution. MiniFast is a modular malware suspected of being generated using artificial intelligence (AI).

malware.name: MiniJunk
malware.description: MiniJunk is a custom malware designed for long-term persistence and remote code execution. MiniJunk was first observed in 2025 and is a modified version of the MiniBike framework that was first observed in June 2022.

malware.name: MirageFox
malware.description: MirageFox is a remote access tool used against Windows systems. It appears to be an upgraded version of a tool known as Mirage, which is a RAT believed to originate in 2012.

malware.name: Mirax

malware.name: MirrorStealer
malware.description: MirrorStealer is a credential stealer that has been used by MirrorFace since at least 2022 to steal credentials from various applications, including browsers and email clients.

malware.name: Mis-Type
malware.description: Mis-Type is a backdoor hybrid that was used in Operation Dust Storm by 2012.

malware.name: Misdat
malware.description: Misdat is a backdoor that was used in Operation Dust Storm from 2010 to 2011.

malware.name: Mispadu
malware.description: Mispadu is a banking trojan written in Delphi that was first observed in 2019 and uses a Malware-as-a-Service (MaaS) business model. This malware is operated, managed, and sold by the Malteiro cybercriminal group.

malware.name: Mivast
malware.description: Mivast is a backdoor that has been used by Deep Panda. It was reportedly used in the Anthem breach.

malware.name: MobileOrder
malware.description: MobileOrder is a Trojan intended to compromise Android mobile devices. It has been used by Scarlet Mimic.

malware.name: MoleNet
malware.description: MoleNet is a downloader tool with backdoor capabilities that has been observed in use since at least 2019.

malware.name: Monero Miner
malware.description: According to ESET, first seen in-the-wild on 26th May, 2017, the malicious mining software is a fork of a legitimate open source Monero CPU miner called xmrig.

malware.name: Moneybird
malware.description: Moneybird is a ransomware variant written in C++ associated with Agrius operations. The name "Moneybird" is contained in the malware's ransom note and as strings in the executable.

malware.name: Mongall
malware.description: Mongall is a backdoor that has been used since at least 2013, including by Aoqin Dragon.

malware.name: MoonWind
malware.description: MoonWind is a remote access tool (RAT) that was used in 2016 to target organizations in Thailand.

malware.name: MOPSLED
malware.description: MOPSLED is a shellcode-based modular backdoor that has been used by China-nexus cyber espionage actors including UNC3886 and APT41.

malware.name: More_eggs
malware.description: More_eggs is a JScript backdoor used by Cobalt Group and FIN6. Its name was given based on the variable "More_eggs" being present in its code.

malware.name: Mori
malware.description: Mori is a backdoor that has been used by MuddyWater since at least January 2022.

malware.name: Mosquito
malware.description: Mosquito is a Win32 backdoor that has been used by Turla. Mosquito is made up of three parts: the installer, the launcher, and the backdoor. The main backdoor is called CommanderDLL and is launched by the loader program.

malware.name: MuddyViper
malware.description: MuddyViper is custom backdoor written in C and C++ used by MuddyWater for command and control (C2) communications and persistence. MuddyViper is loaded by Fooder and sends frequent messages to the C2 server.

malware.name: MultiLayer Wiper
malware.description: MultiLayer Wiper is wiper malware written in .NET associated with Agrius operations. Observed samples of MultiLayer Wiper have an anomalous, future compilation date suggesting possible metadata manipulation.

malware.name: MURKYTOP
malware.description: MURKYTOP is a reconnaissance tool used by Leviathan.

malware.name: Mythic
malware.description: Mythic is an open source, cross-platform post-exploitation/command and control platform. Mythic is designed to "plug-n-play" with various agents and communication channels.

malware.name: Naid
malware.description: Naid is a trojan used by Elderwood to open a backdoor on compromised hosts.

malware.name: NanHaiShu
malware.description: NanHaiShu is a remote access tool and JScript backdoor used by Leviathan. NanHaiShu has been used to target government and private-sector organizations that have relations to the South China Sea dispute.

malware.name: NanoCore
malware.description: NanoCore is a modular remote access tool developed in .NET that can be used to spy on victims and steal information. It has been used by threat actors since 2013.

malware.name: NativeZone
malware.description: NativeZone is the name given collectively to disposable custom Cobalt Strike loaders used by APT29 since at least 2021.

malware.name: NavRAT
malware.description: NavRAT is a remote access tool designed to upload, download, and execute files. It has been observed in attacks targeting South Korea.

malware.name: NBTscan
malware.description: NBTscan is an open source tool that has been used by state groups to conduct internal reconnaissance within a compromised network.

malware.name: nbtstat
malware.description: nbtstat is a utility used to troubleshoot NetBIOS name resolution.

malware.name: NDiskMonitor
malware.description: NDiskMonitor is a custom backdoor written in .NET that appears to be unique to Patchwork.

malware.name: Nebulae
malware.description: Nebulae Is a backdoor that has been used by Naikon since at least 2020.

malware.name: Nefilim
malware.description: According to Vitali Kremez and Michael Gillespie, this ransomware shares much code with Nemty 2.5. A difference is removal of the RaaS component, which was switched to email communications for payments.

malware.name: Neo-reGeorg
malware.description: Neo-reGeorg is an open-source web shell designed as a restructuring of reGeorg with improved usability, security, and fixes for exising reGeorg bugs.

malware.name: Neoichor
malware.description: Neoichor is C2 malware used by Ke3chang since at least 2019; similar malware families used by the group include Leeson and Numbldea.

malware.name: Nerex
malware.description: Nerex is a Trojan used by Elderwood to open a backdoor on compromised hosts.

malware.name: Net
malware.description: The Net utility is a component of the Windows operating system. It is used in command-line operations for control of users, groups, services, and network connections.

malware.name: Net Crawler

malware.name: NETEAGLE
malware.description: NETEAGLE is a backdoor developed by APT30 with compile dates as early as 2008. It has two main variants known as “Scout” and “Norton.”

malware.name: netsh
malware.description: netsh is a scripting utility used to interact with networking components on local or remote systems.

malware.name: netstat
malware.description: netstat is an operating system utility that displays active TCP connections, listening ports, and network statistics.

malware.name: NetSupportManager RAT
malware.description: Enigma Software notes that NetSupport Manager is a genuine application, which was first released about twenty years ago.

malware.name: NetTraveler
malware.description: NetTraveler is malware that has been used in multiple cyber espionage campaigns for basic surveillance of victims.

malware.name: Netwalker
malware.description: Netwalker is fileless ransomware written in PowerShell and executed directly in memory.

malware.name: NETWIRE
malware.description: NETWIRE is a publicly available, multiplatform remote administration tool (RAT) that has been used by criminal and APT groups since at least 2012.

malware.name: NGLite

malware.name: ngrok
malware.description: ngrok is a legitimate reverse proxy tool that can create a secure tunnel to servers located behind firewalls or on local machines that do not have a public IP.

malware.name: NICECURL
malware.description: NICECURL is a VBScript-based backdoor used by APT42 to download additional modules.

malware.name: Nidiran
malware.description: Nidiran is a custom backdoor developed and used by Suckfly. It has been delivered via strategic web compromise.

malware.name: NightClub
malware.description: NightClub is a modular implant written in C++ that has been used by MoustachedBouncer since at least 2014.

malware.name: Nightdoor
malware.description: Nightdoor is a backdoor exclusively associated with Daggerfly operations. Nightdoor uses common libraries with MgBot and MacMa, linking these malware families together.

malware.name: Ninja
malware.description: Ninja is a malware developed in C++ that has been used by ToddyCat to penetrate networks and control remote systems since at least 2020.

malware.name: njRAT
malware.description: njRAT is a remote access tool (RAT) that was first observed in 2012. It has been used by threat actors in the Middle East.

malware.name: NKAbuse
malware.description: NKAbuse is a Go-based, multi-platform malware abusing NKN (New Kind of Network) technology for data exchange between peers, functioning as a potent implant, and equipped with both flooder and backdoor capabilities.

malware.name: Nltest
malware.description: Nltest is a Windows command-line utility used to list domain controllers and enumerate domain trusts.

malware.name: NOKKI
malware.description: NOKKI is a modular remote access tool. The earliest observed attack using NOKKI was in January 2018. NOKKI has significant code overlap with the KONNI malware family.

malware.name: NOOPLDR
malware.description: NOOPLDR is a shellcode loader with XML/C# and DLL versions that has been used by MirrorFace to load HiddenFace.

malware.name: NotPetya

malware.name: NPPSPY
malware.description: NPPSPY is an implementation of a theoretical mechanism first presented in 2004 for capturing credentials submitted to a Windows system via a rogue Network Provider API item.

malware.name: ObliqueRAT
malware.description: ObliqueRAT is a remote access trojan, similar to Crimson, that has been in use by Transparent Tribe since at least 2020.

malware.name: OceanSalt
malware.description: OceanSalt is a Trojan that was used in a campaign targeting victims in South Korea, United States, and Canada. OceanSalt shares code similarity with SpyNote RAT, which has been linked to APT1.

malware.name: Octopus
malware.description: Octopus is a Windows Trojan written in the Delphi programming language that has been used by Nomadic Octopus to target government organizations in Central Asia since at least 2014.

malware.name: ODAgent
malware.description: ODAgent is a C#/.NET downloader that has been used by OilRig since at least 2022 including against target organizations in Israel to download and execute payloads and to exfiltrate staged files.

malware.name: OilBooster
malware.description: OilBooster is a downloader written in Microsoft Visual C/C++ that has been used by OilRig since at least 2022 including against target organizations in Israel to download and execute files and for exfiltration.

malware.name: OilCheck
malware.description: OilCheck is a C#/.NET downloader that has been used by OilRig since at least 2022 including against targets in Israel. OilCheck uses draft messages created in a shared email account for C2 communication.

malware.name: Okrum
malware.description: Okrum is a Windows backdoor that has been seen in use since December 2016 with strong links to Ke3chang.

malware.name: OLDBAIT
malware.description: OLDBAIT is a credential harvester used by APT28.

malware.name: Olympic Destroyer
malware.description: Olympic Destroyer is malware that was used by Sandworm Team against the 2018 Winter Olympics, held in Pyeongchang, South Korea. The main purpose of the malware was to render infected computer systems inoperable.

malware.name: OnionDuke
malware.description: OnionDuke is malware that was used by APT29 from 2013 to 2015.

malware.name: OopsIE
malware.description: OopsIE is a Trojan used by OilRig to remotely execute commands as well as upload/download files to/from victims.

malware.name: OrBit

malware.name: Orz
malware.description: Orz is a custom JavaScript backdoor used by Leviathan. It was observed being used in 2014 as well as in August 2017 when it was dropped by Microsoft Publisher files.

malware.name: OSInfo
malware.description: OSInfo is a custom tool used by APT3 to do internal discovery on a victim's computer and network.

malware.name: OSX_OCEANLOTUS.D
malware.description: OSX_OCEANLOTUS.D is a macOS backdoor used by APT32. First discovered in 2015, APT32 has continued to make improvements using a plugin architecture to extend capabilities, specifically using `.dylib` files.

malware.name: OSX/Shlayer
malware.description: OSX/Shlayer is a Trojan designed to install adware on macOS that was first discovered in 2018.

malware.name: Out1
malware.description: Out1 is a remote access tool written in python and used by MuddyWater since at least 2021.

malware.name: OutSteel
malware.description: OutSteel is a file uploader and document stealer developed with the scripting language AutoIT that has been used by Saint Bear since at least March 2021.

malware.name: OwaAuth
malware.description: OwaAuth is a Web shell and credential stealer deployed to Microsoft Exchange servers that appears to be exclusively used by Threat Group-3390.

malware.name: P.A.S. Webshell
malware.description: P.A.S. Webshell is a publicly available multifunctional PHP webshell in use since at least 2016 that provides remote access and execution on target web servers.

malware.name: P2P ZeuS
malware.description: P2P ZeuS is a closed-source fork of the leaked version of the ZeuS botnet. It presents improvements over the leaked version, including a peer-to-peer architecture.

malware.name: P8RAT
malware.description: P8RAT is a fileless malware used by menuPass to download and execute payloads since at least 2020.

malware.name: PACEMAKER
malware.description: PACEMAKER is a credential stealer that was used by APT5 as early as 2020 including activity against US Defense Industrial Base (DIB) companies.

malware.name: Pacu
malware.description: Pacu is an open-source AWS exploitation framework. The tool is written in Python and publicly available on GitHub.

malware.name: PAKLOG

malware.name: Pandora
malware.description: Pandora is a multistage kernel rootkit with backdoor functionality that has been in use by Threat Group-3390 since at least 2020.

malware.name: Pasam
malware.description: Pasam is a trojan used by Elderwood to open a backdoor on compromised hosts.

malware.name: Pass-The-Hash Toolkit
malware.description: Pass-The-Hash Toolkit is a toolkit that allows an adversary to "pass" a password hash (without knowing the original password) to log in to systems.

malware.name: Pay2Key
malware.description: Pay2Key is a ransomware written in C++ that has been used by Fox Kitten since at least July 2020 including campaigns against Israeli companies.

malware.name: Payload
malware.description: According to 0x3oBAD, this is a 64-bit Linux ELF ransomware binary targeting VMware ESXi hypervisor environments.

malware.name: Pcexter
malware.description: Pcexter is an uploader that has been used by ToddyCat since at least 2023 to exfiltrate stolen files.

malware.name: PcShare
malware.description: PcShare is an open source remote access tool that has been modified and used by Chinese threat actors, most notably during the FunnyDream campaign since late 2018.

malware.name: Peirates
malware.description: Peirates is a post-exploitation Kubernetes exploitation framework with a focus on gathering service account tokens for lateral movement and privilege escalation.

malware.name: Penquin
malware.description: Penquin is a remote access trojan (RAT) with multiple versions used by Turla to target Linux systems since at least 2014.

malware.name: Peppy
malware.description: Peppy is a Python-based remote access Trojan, active since at least 2012, with similarities to Crimson.

malware.name: PHASEJAM

malware.name: PHOREAL
malware.description: PHOREAL is a signature backdoor used by APT32.

malware.name: PHPsert

malware.description: Pillowmint is a point-of-sale malware used by FIN7 designed to capture credit card information.

malware.name: PinchDuke
malware.description: PinchDuke is malware that was used by APT29 from 2008 to 2010.

malware.name: Ping
malware.description: Ping is an operating system utility commonly used to troubleshoot and verify network connections.

malware.name: PingPull
malware.description: PingPull is a remote access Trojan (RAT) written in Visual C++ that has been used by GALLIUM since at least June 2022.

malware.name: PipeMon
malware.description: PipeMon is a multi-stage modular backdoor used by Winnti Group.

malware.name: Pisloader

malware.name: PITSTOP
